# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick: JBL Charge 6** (about $130-$150)
- It has an IP68 rating (dust-tight, submersible), 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and clear, powerful sound. It can also charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and BestProducts did too. Prices listed were $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) · [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Other picks by need**

| Need | Pick | Key points | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pool party, max volume | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats and has 40+ hours of battery. It's large and directional, so sound is muffled off to the side. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Sound all around the pool | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | IP67, 360° sound, floats, 15-hour battery. Tom's Guide's best overall. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) |
| Budget, floats | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | IP67, floats, 14 hours. About $65 on sale at BestProducts. | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip | About $100, IP68, 12 hours, can-shaped. Good Housekeeping's best overall. The mesh can collect dust. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| Cheapest | JBL Go 5 | About $40, IP67, pocket-sized, but only 8 hours of battery. | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Big, loud backyard party | Soundcore Boom 2 Plus | 100 W, floats, up to 20 hours. It's IPX7 with no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. It's heavy at 3.8 kg. Listed at $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20, which Dealectric says it tested at checkout. [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (affiliate link) | [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus) |

**Tips**
- For the pool, look for IP67 or higher, and ideally a speaker that floats.
- For the beach, you also want dust protection (the first number in the IP rating should be 5 or 6).
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. RTINGS recommends rinsing with fresh water after use, and you should check your model's manual first. Keep the charging port closed and let the speaker dry before charging.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow it to one.
